passage: In the school library, Chandrika pretended to read but watched the corner table. Four girls had their heads together. "Don't tell anyone, okay?" one whispered, and the story moved from ear to ear like a passed note. Amandeep sat at the edge, not part of the group usually. She leaned in, listened, then added, "I heard that too," though Chandrika was sure she hadn't. The girls turned to her, smiling, and made space on the bench. Amandeep's shoulders relaxed. When the librarian came past, they all went silent and opened their books. Chandrika looked at the table of whispering heads and wondered who in there actually knew anything, and who just wanted to belong.

qa.q: Where was Chandrika watching the girls from?
qa.a: Chandrika was in the school library, pretending to read.

qa.q: Why might Amandeep have said "I heard that too"?
qa.a: She probably wanted to be included, and joining in the story made the girls smile and make space for her.

qa.q: How could a teacher or librarian gently interrupt this chain?
qa.a: They could talk with the group later about how whispered stories hurt the person in them, and help Amandeep find other ways to be included.

qa.q: What would change if Amandeep had not joined in?
qa.a: She might have stayed on the edge of the bench, but the story would have had one less person carrying it.

grounding: It shows an onlooker watching a secret passed in whispers with "don't tell anyone" and a listener repeating it to be included.

passage: I'm Aparna, and I sit behind Akash in class 6. On Monday I saw the whole thing. Rinku leaned over to Akash during drawing period and whispered something, then said, "Swear you won't tell." Akash swore. By lunch, he was whispering it to Farhan and Joel, with the same "swear you won't tell." He looked happy, like he was finally in their gang. Joel laughed and gave him half his samosa. By the last bell, I think half the class knew, and every single person had sworn not to tell. I don't know if Akash even believed it. Maybe he just liked that everyone was leaning in to listen to him for once.

qa.q: What did Joel give Akash at lunch?
qa.a: Joel gave him half his samosa.

qa.q: What does Aparna think Akash was feeling when he passed the story on?
qa.a: Aparna thinks he felt happy and included, like he was finally part of the gang, and liked people leaning in to listen to him.

qa.q: What could Akash do next time someone makes him swear to keep a story?
qa.a: He could keep it to himself, or ask if it is kind or true, and find other ways, like games or shared lunch, to join the group.

qa.q: How might Rinku feel seeing the secret spread across the class?
qa.a: Rinku may feel let down and embarrassed, since Rinku made Akash swear not to tell and by the last bell half the class knew.

grounding: It illustrates a classmate observing a story spread with sworn secrecy, and a boy repeating it to feel part of the group.

passage:
Monday. Mehak watched the whisper start at the back bench. Sonal leaned to Tina: "Don't tell anyone, but Rinku's father lost his job." Tina's eyes went round.

Tuesday. At lunch the whisper had reached the girls by the window. Mehak heard it again, with an extra part: "and they're selling their car." Each person said, "Promise you won't tell," and then told.

Wednesday. Jatin, who usually sat alone, leaned over to Mehak's group. "Did you hear about Rinku? They're selling their house too." The group turned to him, surprised, and let him sit with them for the first time.

Mehak saw his face light up. He wasn't saying it to be mean, she thought. He was saying it so they'd let him in.

Rinku, two rows ahead, was colouring her map, not knowing.

qa.q: What extra part had been added by Tuesday?
qa.a: "And they're selling their car."

qa.q: What does Mehak think about why Jatin joined in?
qa.a: She feels uneasy but understanding, believing he repeated it not to be mean but to be let into the group.

qa.q: What could Mehak do to stop the chain?
qa.a: She could refuse to pass it on and quietly tell her group it's Rinku's private matter, or tell a teacher if it keeps spreading.

qa.q: How might Rinku feel if she knew what was being whispered?
qa.a: She would probably feel embarrassed and hurt, especially since some parts, like the house, may not even be true.

grounding: Mehak watches a rumour travel in "don't tell anyone" whispers, and sees Jatin repeat it to feel part of the group.

passage:
Kavitha, you don't know whether to join the whispering about the new girl? Let your Jagdish dadu tell you what I saw in my village school.

A boy named Bhola came to our class from the city. Someone said his mother had run away. Nobody knew if it was true. But everyone whispered, "Don't tell anyone," and then told everyone.

I watched my friend Mohan, who was always left out of games. One day he whispered it too, louder than anyone. The big boys laughed and let him play kabaddi with them that evening.

I understood then. Mohan didn't care about Bhola's mother. He wanted to belong.

The turning point, Kavitha, came when our teacher heard it and sat us all down. Bhola's mother was working in Delhi. I've never forgotten Bhola's face that week.

qa.q: Where was Bhola's mother actually?
qa.a: Working in Delhi.

qa.q: What did young Jagdish realise about why Mohan repeated the rumour?
qa.a: He realised, with some sadness, that Mohan didn't care about the story; he felt left out and wanted to belong.

qa.q: What was the turning point in the story?
qa.a: When the teacher heard the rumour and sat the class down, showing the truth about Bhola's mother.

qa.q: How do you think Bhola felt that week?
qa.a: He was probably hurt, lonely and ashamed, as the new boy whispered about by everyone.

grounding: Jagdish dadu recalls watching a rumour spread with "don't tell anyone" and seeing a left-out boy repeat it to belong.

passage:
The bus was stuck in traffic for forty minutes after school, so the whispering had plenty of time to travel.

Himani, in the window seat, watched it go from the back row forward. "Don't tell anyone, but Sweety's brother got caught cheating in his exam." Each child leaned to the next. "Promise you won't tell." Then they told.

When it reached Jeevan, the quiet boy in the seat across the aisle, Himani expected him to shrug. Instead he turned to the boys in front and said, "I heard he's getting thrown out of college, even." They turned around, interested. One of them offered Jeevan a chip.

Jeevan grinned. It was the first time anyone on the bus had shared with him.

Himani looked at Sweety, sitting near the front with her headphones in, and felt her stomach twist.

qa.q: How long was the bus stuck in traffic?
qa.a: Forty minutes.

qa.q: What was Himani feeling when she looked at Sweety?
qa.a: Her stomach twisted; she felt uneasy and sorry for Sweety, who didn't know what was being said.

qa.q: What small step could Himani take?
qa.a: She could refuse to pass it on and, if it keeps spreading, tell a teacher, since it is about Sweety's family.

qa.q: Why might Jeevan have joined in so eagerly?
qa.a: He was usually left out, and repeating the rumour, even adding to it, made the other boys include him.

grounding: On a stuck bus Himani watches a rumour travel with "promise you won't tell", and sees a left-out boy repeat it to belong.

passage:
In Class 5B of a Delhi school, the story travelled from desk to desk like a folded chit. "Don't tell anyone," Dolma whispered to Pranav during art, "but Ritesh failed and has to repeat the year."
Pranav nodded. He watched it move: Dolma told the twins, the twins told Aman, and every telling began with "promise you won't say". Pranav noticed that the whisperers leaned together like a club. He had never been in that club.
At recess, when Aman and the twins huddled near the swings, Pranav walked up and said, "I heard it too. About Ritesh."
They made room for him at once. He felt warm, included, and a little sick, all at the same time.

qa.q: How did every telling of the story begin?
qa.a: Every telling began with "promise you won't say".

qa.q: How did Pranav feel when the group made room for him?
qa.a: He felt warm and included, and at the same time a little sick, because he had joined in by repeating the story.

qa.q: What could Pranav have done at the swings instead of repeating the story?
qa.a: He could have joined the group with something else to talk about, or said he didn't want to pass it on, since belonging does not have to cost Ritesh.

qa.q: What is it like for Ritesh while the whisper travels around 5B?
qa.a: Ritesh may notice huddles and glances without knowing why, and feel uneasy or left out as the story grows behind his back.

grounding: Shows a whispered story spreading with promises of secrecy, and a listener repeating it to feel part of the group.
